observation.visible_scene: A square loop made of a lumpy yellowish material (like a foam- or wire-covered frame) hangs against a pure black background, holding a thin horizontal film. The film shows interference colors: a silvery-white upper zone riddled with black speckles and faint swirling streaks, a transitional orange/amber band, a vivid blue-violet iridescent band near the bottom, and a pale silvery strip at the very bottom edge. Above the film's top boundary is a dark (black) region with a thin wavy meniscus line.
visible_changes: The square loop and the black background remain essentially fixed in position from first to last frame, so the apparent changes are within the film, not camera motion.

For the first ~0.7 s the film's overall layout (vertical streaks, orange and blue bands) is broadly stable, with only slow drifting/rearranging of the black speckles and subtle shifts of the swirl patterns.

Around t≈0.73–0.80 s a thin vertical line/channel appears near the horizontal centre of the film, running from the top boundary down to the lower edge, where a small dark droplet forms; this vertical seam persists through the rest of the excerpt.

After the vertical line forms, the blue-violet band reorganises around it (the colour bands deform, e.g. a downward notch/V-shape appears at the centre bottom in mid-frames, then relaxes toward a wavy horizontal band again), and the black speckles continue to redistribute.
The orange band and the upper silvery zone gradually change texture and brightness but do not translate as a rigid object; the changes are local deformations of the film pattern.
The top dark region and its wavy meniscus boundary stay present throughout, with only minor shape changes.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the vertical channel (drainage, film thinning, or an external disturbance) is not shown; the excerpt begins mid-process.
Whether the film will rupture, drain further, or stabilise after the last frame is unknown.
The identity of the frame material and the film liquid is not determinable from the images.
uncertain_details: Whether the vertical line is a true seam dividing two film regions or a thinning/drainage channel cannot be confirmed.
Any tiny wobble of the yellow loop is at the limit of visibility and may be camera jitter rather than object motion.
Exact timing of the vertical line's onset is approximate (between the t≈0.67 s and t≈0.80 s samples).
